question: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the physician for the evaluation of back pain for the past six months. The pain is worse with exercise and when reclining. He attends high school and is on the swim team. He also states that he lifts weights on a regular basis. He has not had any trauma to the back or any previous problems with his joints. He has no history of serious illness. His father has a disc herniation. Palpation of the spinous processes at the lumbosacral area shows that two adjacent vertebrae are displaced and are at different levels. Muscle strength is normal. Sensation to pinprick and light touch is intact throughout. When the patient is asked to walk, a waddling gait is noted. Passive raising of either the right or left leg causes pain radiating down the ipsilateral leg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Weightlifting and swimming -> increased risk of back injury -> potential for musculoskeletal strain -> 70% CHAIN: Back pain worse with exercise and reclining -> suggests mechanical stress on the back -> possible structural issue -> 60% CHAIN: Palpation reveals displaced vertebrae at different levels -> indicative of spondylolisthesis -> 80% CHAIN: Waddling gait noted during walking -> sign of nerve compression -> consistent with spondylolisthesis -> 85% CHAIN: Pain radiating down ipsilateral leg with passive leg raising -> indicative of nerve root impingement -> supports spondylolisthesis diagnosis -> 90% CHAIN: Most likely diagnosis is Spondylolisthesis -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 14-year-old boy with back pain, displaced vertebrae, waddling gait, and pain radiating down the leg is Spondylolisthesis. The evidence of displaced vertebrae at different levels on palpation, waddling gait indicating nerve compression, and pain radiating down the leg with passive leg raising support this diagnosis.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for the 14-year-old boy with back pain, displaced vertebrae, waddling gait, and pain radiating down the leg is Spondylolisthesis. The presence of displaced vertebrae at different levels on palpation, waddling gait indicating nerve compression, and pain radiating down the leg with passive leg raising are classic signs of spondylolisthesis.
